questions.text:
A Young tableau is a 2D array of integers increasing from left to right and from top to bottom. Any unfilled entries are marked with [latex]\infty[/latex], and hence there cannot be any entry to the right of, or below a [latex]\infty[/latex]. The following Young tableau consists of unique entries.

When an element is removed from a Young tableau, other elements should be moved into its place so that the resulting table is still a Young tableau (unfilled entries may be filled in with a [latex]\infty[/latex]). The minimum number of entries (other than 1) to be shifted, to remove 1 from the given Young tableau is _______.
questions.solution:
Removing 1 leaves a hole. Repeatedly fill it with the smaller of its right and lower neighbour:

- hole (1,1): min(2, 3) = 2 moves left
- hole (1,2): min(5, 4) = 4 moves up
- hole (2,2): min(6, 12) = 6 moves left
- hole (2,3): min(23, 18) = 18 moves up
- hole (3,3): min(25, [latex]\infty[/latex]) = 25 moves left
- hole (3,4) gets [latex]\infty[/latex]

Shifted: 2, 4, 6, 18, 25 = 5 entries

Answer: 5

questions.text:
Given below are some algorithms, and some algorithm design paradigms.

Match the above algorithms on the left to the corresponding design paradigm they follow.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Dijkstra: greedy (iii)
- Floyd-Warshall: dynamic programming (ii)
- Binary search: divide and conquer (i)
- Backtracking: depth-first search (iv)

Answer: 1-iii, 2-ii, 3-i, 4-iv

questions.text: Consider two decision problems Q1,Q2 such that Q1 reduces in polynomial time to 3-SAT and 3-SAT reduces in polynomial time to Q2. Then which one of the following is consistent with the above statement?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Q1 [latex]\le_p[/latex] 3-SAT, and 3-SAT is in NP [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q1 is in NP.
- 3-SAT [latex]\le_p[/latex] Q2, and 3-SAT is NP-hard [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Q2 is NP-hard.

Answer: Q1 is in NP, Q2 is NP hard

questions.text: The graph shown below has 8 edges with distinct integer edge weights. The minimum spanning tree (MST) is of weight 36 and contains the edges: {(A, C), (B, C), (B, E), (E, F), (D, F)}. The edge weights of only those edges which are in the MST are given in the figure shown below. The minimum possible sum of weights of all 8 edges of this graph is ___________.
questions.solution:
MST weights: AC = 9, BC = 2, BE = 15, EF = 4, DF = 6 (total 36). A non-MST edge must be heavier than every MST edge on its cycle (weights are distinct).

- AB: cycle A-C-B, max 9 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] AB [latex]\ge[/latex] 10
- CD: path C-B-E-F-D, max 15 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CD [latex]\ge[/latex] 16
- DE: path D-F-E, max 6 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] DE [latex]\ge[/latex] 7

Minimum total = 36 + 10 + 16 + 7 = 69

Answer: 69
